final_codebook.domain: Subtraction of fractions, mixed numbers, and whole numbers, including equivalent-form preparation, denominator alignment, regrouping, and simplification

skills.name: Normalize operands
skills.definition: Rewrite a whole number or nonstandard mixed number into an equivalent subtraction-ready form without changing its value.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a whole number is rewritten as a whole plus 0/d to support subtraction with a fraction or mixed number.
Tag when a mixed number with an improper fractional part is converted to an equivalent standard mixed number.
Tag when a fractional part inside a mixed number is simplified before subtraction to create an equivalent easier form.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag finding or applying a common denominator between two fractions.
Do not tag ordinary subtraction once quantities are already in usable form.
Do not tag borrowing/regrouping after subtraction has begun.
Do not tag final simplification of the result unless the step is rewriting an operand before subtraction.

skills.name: Create common denominator
skills.definition: Find a common denominator and convert one or more fractions to equivalent fractions with matching denominators before subtraction.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a step explicitly finds an LCD or common denominator.
Tag when one or both fractions are rewritten as equivalent fractions to match denominators.
Tag for denominator alignment in pure-fraction items or in the fractional parts of mixed numbers.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when denominators are already compatible and no conversion is actually performed.
Do not tag rewriting a whole number as a whole plus 0/d.
Do not tag converting an improper mixed number to a standard mixed number.
Do not tag numerator subtraction itself.

skills.name: Subtract aligned parts
skills.definition: Subtract fractions with like denominators and/or subtract whole-number and fractional parts once the quantities are in compatible form, then combine those parts when no regrouping or simplification is the main operation.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when numerators are subtracted over a shared denominator.
Tag when whole parts of mixed numbers are subtracted.
Tag when fraction parts of mixed numbers are subtracted after normalization or denominator alignment.
Tag when the solver combines already-subtracted whole and fractional parts into the stated result, provided regrouping or simplification is not the main purpose of the step.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag steps whose main purpose is to create a common denominator or otherwise rewrite operands into equivalent forms.
Do not tag borrowing or regrouping used because the fractional subtraction would be negative.
Do not tag simplification to lowest terms or conversion of 0/d to 0 when no subtraction is performed in that step.

skills.name: Regroup and simplify
skills.definition: Borrow one whole into fractional units when needed and express the resulting answer in simplest valid form, including reducing fractions or removing zero-fraction forms.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when 1 whole is borrowed and converted into denominator-over-denominator fractional units.
Tag when regrouping resolves a negative fractional difference in mixed-number or whole-minus-fraction subtraction.
Tag when a reducible fraction is simplified after subtraction.
Tag when 0/d or a zero-fraction mixed number is simplified to an integer or whole-number form.
Tag when the final whole and fractional parts are combined in a step whose main purpose is completing a regrouped or simplified result.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag straightforward subtraction that requires no regrouping and no simplification.
Do not tag initial operand normalization before subtraction.
Do not tag ordinary combining of parts when no regrouping or simplification is involved.

decisions.reasoning: Both candidates concern equivalent-form preparation before subtraction. In the item set, rewriting a whole number as a mixed form and converting a nonstandard mixed number to standard form are not independently strong enough to justify separate skills, and A/B already treat them as one coherent normalization process. Merging improves minimality and identifiability while preserving clear boundaries from denominator work and regrouping.

Creating a common denominator is a distinct, independently testable operation that appears in both pure-fraction and mixed-number items. It should remain separate from normalization and from subtraction itself under the non-redundancy principle.

The dossiers and expert codebooks show that fraction subtraction and mixed/whole-part subtraction are usually the same underlying execution phase: subtracting already-aligned components. Splitting them would reduce independence because many mixed-number items require both together, while A and B consistently model them as one broader subtraction skill. The merged skill still remains distinct from setup and regrouping.

decisions.details: Refined S03 to exclude regrouping-driven completion and standalone simplification
decisions.reasoning: This sharper boundary improves annotation agreement: S03 covers ordinary subtraction and combination after setup, while S04 handles cases where regrouping or simplification is the main cognitive demand.

decisions.details: Kept C06 as S04 with refined wording
decisions.reasoning: All experts agreed on this concept. Although borrowing and simplification are separable in theory, they are combined in the source codebooks and often occur in the same late-stage resolution phase in this item set. Keeping them together preserves consensus and supports a 4-skill codebook.

decisions.details: Refined S04 to explicitly include simplifying 0/d to 0 and final combination after regrouping/simplification
decisions.reasoning: Several dossier steps show that the final accepted form is produced as part of the regroup/simplify phase. Making this explicit improves completeness and reduces ambiguity with S03.

summary: The final 4-skill codebook preserves the strongest cross-expert consensus while consolidating granularity differences. Operand normalization and improper-mixed-number cleanup were merged into one preparation skill; common-denominator work was kept separate; fraction subtraction and mixed/whole-part subtraction were merged into one execution skill; and borrowing plus simplification were retained as a final resolution skill with clearer boundaries.
